Norway Imposes Import Tariffs on Retail Goods, Industry Reports Supply Strains

OSLO, June 13—Norway’s government has imposed new tariffs of up to 18 percent on a wide range of imported retail goods, sparking concerns among retailers nationwide over shrinking margins, supply disruptions, and job security.

The measure, announced last week and taking immediate effect, targets clothing, electronics, and household products sourced from outside the European Economic Area. Retailers say the move has led to immediate price increases on shelves and mounting pressure on local inventory.

“We’re already seeing the impact,” said Erik Johansson, Chief Executive at Nordicon Retail Group, which operates more than 120 stores nationwide. “Certain popular items are selling out faster, and the cost to restock is considerably higher than before.”

Industry associations warn that the tariffs threaten the viability of smaller retail businesses. “Independent retailers, especially in rural areas, are struggling to absorb these costs and may be forced to lay off staff or reduce hours,” said Anja Lunde, spokesperson for the Norwegian Retail Federation. She estimated that as many as 3,000 jobs could be at risk if the tariffs remain in place through the summer.

At several large city-center retail sites, managers have reported a slowdown in foot traffic as shoppers react to higher prices. “We’re doing what we can to keep prices down, but it’s difficult,” said Ingrid Madsen, who manages a chain of electronics outlets in Oslo. “Staff are worried about the future.”

Government officials say the move is intended to support domestic retail competitiveness, but industry representatives are calling for urgent dialogue to mitigate ongoing impacts.
